A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Arithmetic-GPT research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and human-choice data analyses, including model comparisons, embedding analyses, and cross-validation results in Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds empirical comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and arithmetic evaluations in Tables A2–A5 and Figures A1–A3.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains arithmetic pretraining followed by frozen final-layer embeddings and logistic regression on human choices. The main architecture, objective, and synthetic-data construction are unchanged. Smaller models and alternative distributions are sensitivity settings, without a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The same four human datasets and risky/intertemporal decision domains remain. Appendix B/Table A2 newly includes choices13k trials with feedback, which v1 excluded. The additional synthetic tests and distribution variants remain within expected-value arithmetic rather than introducing another domain.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds LLaMA3 text-derived embeddings and logistic regression on exact expected-value differences, supplying important representation and rational-choice controls absent from v1. The text-embedding comparator also enters cross-validation in Table A1. Existing comparators remain; CPT is relabeled prospect theory with unchanged equations and scores.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds systematic experiments crossing model sizes of 10M, 1M, and 30K parameters with 1M, 100K, and 10K equations, plus independently varied probability/value distributions. Appendix G introduces two 20K-equation tests, using two-decimal answer probabilities for Arithmetic-GPT and temperature-zero integer-answer accuracy for LLaMA3. These substantially extend evaluation design; the original training and cross-validation protocols remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's sign-corruption ablations and cross-validation, v2 adds capacity, data-quantity, and distribution sensitivity studies; implicit-function comparisons for LLaMA3 and other pretraining variants; learning-curve and arithmetic-error diagnostics; and feedback-inclusive robustness evaluation. Appendices C, E, F, and G substantially expand evidence about dependencies and possible mechanisms.

E5.justification: Both versions already report means and standard errors over ten random train/validation splits. v2 adds significance-based highlighting at the 0.05 level in Tables A1 and A3, without specifying the test. It does not establish an increased repeat count; changed standard-error values are result revisions.

E6.justification: Existing Table 3 scores remain unchanged, but new comparator results include 98.0% R2 for LLaMA3 text embeddings on agrawal23. From v1 Table 4 to v2 Table A1, choices13k cross-validation changes from 55.9% to 56.4% for uniform pretraining and 56.1% to 57.7% for ecological pretraining, with revised standard errors. Tables A2–A5 and Figures A1–A3 add substantial findings, including largely preserved 10M-model performance with only 10K training equations.

T1.justification: The EV/PV, utility, probability-weighting, and hyperbolic-discount definitions in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added. Appendix G's conditional-probability notation explains evaluation scoring rather than introducing new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: ecological arithmetic pretraining produces representations that predict human risky and intertemporal choices, motivating controlled pretraining-data ablations. The explicit wording about independence from natural-language supervision clarifies the existing arithmetic-only sufficiency claim.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes probing computational problems from directly modeling human cognitive processes, acknowledges reduced versatility and unrealistic training experience, and qualifies comparisons with LLaMA3. It adds interpretations concerning capacity, numerical distributions, and possible burstiness effects, while acknowledging that arithmetic ability does not straightforwardly explain embeddings' predictive power. These materially expand applicability boundaries and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies adjusted R2 versus squared Pearson correlation, specifies min–max normalization, and documents the new experiments' hidden sizes, distribution parameters, decoding temperature, and answer extraction. Main implementation details and hardware remain unchanged; v1 Appendix C is retained as Appendix H. No new code or data access information appears.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. and Hagendorff et al. to qualify human–LLM behavioral similarities, and Chan et al. to motivate the burstiness interpretation. The broader positioning relative to cognitive models, synthetic pretraining, and rational-choice theories remains stable. The bibliography's author–year conversion is stylistic.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are preserved. Changes include more precise language-model terminology, CPT-to-prospect-theory relabeling, dataset-name correction, local explanatory edits, and author–year citations. New appendix sections are inserted and implementation details move from C to H, without extensive restructuring of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures A1–A3 and Tables A2–A5, expands Tables 3 and A1, and adopts the ICLR layout with revised typography and headers. The former Table 4 becomes Table A1. Figure 1 is also edited: its new expression '16-1*0.6+40*0.4' incorrectly represents the illustrated expected-value difference.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny: the added text-embedding and EV controls address missing comparisons, while the capacity, data-size, distribution, and embedding analyses test dependencies left unresolved in v1. Clearer cognitive-modeling limitations also improve interpretation. Table A5's different correctness measures prevent a direct Arithmetic-GPT/LLaMA3 accuracy comparison, and Figure 1 introduces an arithmetic error. These weaknesses limit particular additions but do not outweigh the substantial gains in controls, sensitivity evidence, and qualification.
